findings.description: The security group allows SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing administrative access to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or credential-stuffing attacks against the instance.

The security group allows HTTP (port 80) from 0.0.0.0/0 with no TLS or compensating controls, exposing the web service to unrestricted access and transmitting any data in cleartext, subject to interception.

AWS access key ID and secret access key are hard-coded in plaintext in the instance user_data script, which is visible via the EC2 instance metadata service and stored in Terraform state, risking credential leakage and compromise of the associated AWS account.

The instance is deployed into a public subnet (map_public_ip_on_launch = true) and attached to a security group permitting SSH and HTTP from anywhere, directly exposing the instance and its embedded plaintext AWS credentials to internet-based attack.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPs to all instances launched in this subnet, increasing the attack surface by default for any workload placed there.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPs to all instances launched in this subnet, increasing the attack surface by default for any workload placed there.

The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, so data written to the volume (and any snapshots derived from it) is stored unencrypted at rest, exposing sensitive data if the underlying storage is compromised.

The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration (e.g., aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration), leaving potentially sensitive network traffic metadata unencrypted at rest.
No public access block, bucket policy, or ACL restrictions are defined for the bucket; combined with force_destroy = true, this raises the risk of unauthorized access or exposure of flow log data.
Egress rule allows all traffic (protocol -1, all ports) to 0.0.0.0/0, providing no network segmentation and allowing unrestricted data exfiltration from a compromised instance.
